jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create an ORIGINAL professional mecha design illustration board for five rescue vehicles from the novel 万机残响, Starfire Five Vehicles. VEHICLE FORMS ONLY in this image, exactly five distinct vehicles, no robots standing, no combined robot yet.
Reference image 1 and 2 are the project's adopted mature mechanical illustration style and depth: hand-drawn dark ink contour with fine mechanical drawing, complex but legible load-bearing shape, convincing three-dimensional mass, restrained edge wear, adult collector mecha art, quiet warm-paper backdrop. Reference 3 shows how a stylized off-road vehicle has strong designed body shapes and purposeful large features; borrow its form clarity, do not copy the RV Robo vehicles or trademarks. Reference 4 is the old accepted medical design for its long patient capsule and white/teal family only. Reference 5 is the accepted tow robot/vehicle for the navy/white family and twin recovery arms only, not its specific shape. None of the letters, labels or humanoid poses in the references belong on the new board.

Wide landscape composition, clean warm ivory background, five LARGE separate complete vehicles presented at consistent front-left three-quarter angles with all vehicle ends in frame. Arrange two large vehicles in the upper row and three in the lower row, generous separation, clear display like a serious Japanese mecha development plate. No labels, numbers, logos, callouts, letters, watermarks, inset robots, extra vehicles or scenery. Each object occupies a substantial area; prioritize five excellent distinct silhouettes over tiny detail.

Common design language: engineered rescue machines for a giant-robot world, 1990s Japanese transforming heroic vehicle aesthetic reinterpreted in sophisticated contemporary ink-and-paint concept art. Broad bold planar shells, strongly designed grille/bumper faces, dark recessed glazing, large real tires, angular but plausible fenders, structural brackets and a few convincing articulated joints. Not ordinary stock trucks, not racing sports cars. Painted steel illustrated with controlled cel-shadow planes, nuanced dark linework, modest painted-metal depth and sparse wear. Avoid glossy 3D toy render, clay, flat vector icons, rounded toddler trucks, chibi proportions, thin doodle line, excessive greeble or glowing sci-fi strips.

The five identities:
TOP LEFT — heavy recovery tow unit: compact broad navy-and-steel-white cab with rust-red small service accents, a powerful low grille and wide bumper, 3 axles / 6 tires total. Behind the cab TWO large separately articulated dark-blue recovery arms fold symmetrically, with heavy pivot sockets and a central winch drum; these distinctive arms will later form the combined robot's shoulder yoke. It looks like the strong short powerful member, not a flatbed truck.
TOP RIGHT — cargo transport unit: long low slate-blue and steel-white cab, 4 axles / 8 tires total, genuinely long open flat cargo deck with thick navy folding side rails, an uninterrupted dark load floor and two rear loading ramps. Keep useful loading space. Its deck will later form a large back platform, not disappear into armor. Broad squared wheel housings and a low planted stance.
BOTTOM LEFT — fire unit: rich rescue red with narrow white bands and dark navy undersides, 3 axles / 6 tires total. An assertive sloped cab, a low protected water tank, two RED broad protective panels folded along the tank, and TWO parallel compact silver/black water-cannon booms stowed longitudinally along the back; these panels can unfold into shoulder/back shield wings. Strong horizontal lamp bar, industrial hose couplings, not a generic cylindrical fuel truck, no huge rooftop ladder.
BOTTOM CENTER — engineering crane unit: saturated construction ochre-yellow, dark navy undercarriage, selective steel-white cab face, 4 axles / 8 tires total, wide low stable chassis with FOUR stout folding outrigger legs visibly retracted along the side sills. One substantial articulated telescoping crane boom folded rearward along the top, with stowed hook. Distinct broad double-lobed chassis volumes that can later make two thick lower legs and blocky boots. It is the wide grounded weight carrier, different from the tow truck.
BOTTOM RIGHT — Bailing medical unit: pearl-white shell with DEEP teal broad lower band and navy structural belly, a long low protected patient capsule on 4 axles / 8 tires total. A striking sophisticated forward wedge cab and a LARGE uninterrupted horizontal patient compartment, not a small ambulance van. A broad side access door in the capsule with a visible robust sliding perimeter seam and two small warm service lamps; a broad dark window band ABOVE the accessible patient floor. The capsule remains a complete horizontal room when combined; its broad outer doors and protective white/teal rim will become the hero robot's main transverse chest armor. The door is CLOSED here, clean and confident, no cross-shaped hospital logo needed. A folded patient-loading platform below the side door, secured and compact.

All five must feel like teammates with unique roles and deliberate transformation-ready large parts, rendered at the same skilled mature level as references 1 and 2. Strong silhouette, attractive sculptural body volumes, credible wheel contact, accurate perspective and sufficient quiet surfaces. This is a design proposal, not a technical blueprint.

jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create the NEXT development plate for exactly the SAME FIVE Starfire rescue machines in reference image 1, now in their FIVE SEPARATE HUMANOID WORKING FORMS. This is not the combined giant. Preserve the exact vehicle identities, body colors, windows, side panel silhouettes, wheel types, recovery arms, deck, fire cannon panels, crane, and medical capsule established in image 1. Reference images 2 and 3 set the mature project illustration quality: deeply drawn structural forms, fine dark ink, subtle painted-steel wear, powerful adult collector mecha silhouettes, strong sculptural volume, controlled hard shadows on warm paper. Reference 4 is only inspiration for how five independently transforming work robots have different body proportions, and must NOT be copied in shape or toy surface. Do not render the toy plastic reference style.

Wide landscape professional concept art plate; FIVE complete standing robots, two on the top row and three on the bottom row, generous visual separation and all feet included. Same reading order as reference 1: top left towing, top right transport; bottom left fire, bottom center engineering, bottom right Bailing medical. Slight front-three-quarter poses, full body and carried structures entirely in frame. Quiet ivory backdrop, sparse ground shadows, no environment, no people, no diagram lines, no text, no letters, no labels, no numbers, no logos. The five should be attractive heroic individuals, with adult 7.5-to-8-head body proportions and small well-designed helmets. They are NOT five recolors of one frame. No round baby shoulders, no chibi heads, no toy render, no smooth white appliance armor, no extremely complex random greebles.

1 TOWING: navy and steel-white, small muted rescue-red blocks, squat powerful silhouette relative to teammates but full mature heroic proportions. Massive thick forearms, wide shoulder cowl formed from the front cab fenders, deep-set angular face in a strong navy recovery helmet. The two long dark-blue recovery arms from the truck are both preserved as a recognizable articulated YOKE folded upward and backward behind shoulders, with bronze/dark pivot sockets and central cable winch. Three axle-pairs worth of large tires remain as shoulder/hip/calf outer details. Large wedge boots, a dark narrow waist and chest face built from the stout grille. Mechanical power, not friendliness.
2 TRANSPORT: tallest leanest teammate, slate navy and steel-white. Long calf volumes, upright architectural shoulder outline, amber side beacons beside a compact serious helmet. Its long empty cargo deck remains a real deck: folded at its structural hinge into a broad stacked back panel and a horizontal shoulder-level LOAD PLATFORM; the two long rear loading ramps remain clearly visible behind it. Cargo floor and side rails can still be recognized, no butterfly wings and no magical extra armor. Ten large tires total may be partly occluded but the distinctive axle assemblies are retained on the outside of the thighs/shins/back frame. Hands strong and simple, front cab becomes a unified pectoral shell with dark rectangular glazing.
3 FIRE: rich rescue red, selective steel white and navy. A muscular upper body distinct from towing: actual curved water-tank portions form broad chest-side volumes and armored upper arms. The exact two red protective panels from its truck unfold slightly behind the shoulders as solid heat-shield fins, with BOTH silver-black water cannons stowed back along them. Compact red and dark visor helmet with a protective central ridge, not a Gundam crown. Six wheels total distributed as substantial knee/calf/back details. Thick red shins, heavy dark wedge feet, one open hand and one relaxed fist. Heroic firefighter presence, no handheld gun.
4 ENGINEERING: ochre-yellow and deep navy, strongest planted lower body. Thick broad lower legs and very wide squared boots visibly made from its low chassis; the FOUR engineering stabilizer legs are folded along calf outer edges / heel supports. The substantial yellow telescoping crane boom remains folded behind the torso and over one shoulder with the same visible secured hook. Yellow construction helmet with broad angular cheek guards and small dark eyes. Dark mechanical waist and silver-white upper thighs, broad yellow shoulder blocks, powerful dexterous hands. Six tires total remain integrated in lower-leg/back outer assemblies. No extra drill bits or excavator buckets.
5 BAILING MEDICAL: white armor, deep teal large panels, dark navy inner structure. Graceful but formidable professional medical responder, lean efficient torso, strong precision forearms and long stable boots, angular protective white/teal helmet with low bright horizontal sensor slit and layered cheek plates; not a cute nurse robot. Her patient capsule MUST remain one intact sealed HORIZONTAL room with an unbroken patient floor and the same wide dark window band, side access doors, teal lower stripe, warm door lamps, and long white side walls from reference 1. Carry this complete capsule horizontally across a well-supported upper-back/shoulder cradle, clearly readable and not sliced into limbs or dangling vertically. Its lower mobile chassis separates to form the robot's long sturdy legs and forearm patient-loading supports, retaining the wheel bogies. One forearm carries a folded broad patient-support tray with a clearly stowed edge; hands are dexterous. CLOSED capsule doors here, no hospital cross logo.

Follow the actual reference vehicle identities, not the earlier prompt's planned axle counts. If a wheel or back panel is hidden by the pose, keep the external silhouette honest; do not create visible duplicate wheels to decorate every joint. Keep the BIG shapes and each machine's memorable working equipment dominant. A convincing adult illustrated mecha team, strong color zoning and handsome faces/helmets, not flat technical icons.

jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a major HERO MECHA DESIGN PORTRAIT of STARFIRE TITAN, the ORIGINAL combined form of exactly the five rescue machines in reference images 1 and 2. This is a new cohesive iconic Japanese transforming rescue-hero robot, with the mature powerful sculptural drawing quality of reference 3. Do not copy their face, chest ornament or color layout. Reference 4 and 5 are official RV/VRV Robo products and are ONLY visual lessons in an iconic horizontal chest symbol, compact helmet, wide shoulders, narrowed waist, huge lower legs/boots, and controlled block-color composition. Do NOT reproduce their exact robot, numbered decorations, toy texture or round lamp pattern.

Reference 1 is the locked five vehicles, reference 2 their five humanoid working forms. THEIR SPECIFIC large parts and colors must remain the source of this combined body. No first-draft Starfire designs are involved. Exactly five constituent identities: navy/white twin-arm tow unit, navy/white open cargo transporter, red fire unit with two wing-shields and two silver-black water cannons, yellow/navy engineering crane with folded stabilizers, and white/teal Bailing medical vehicle with an INTACT horizontal patient capsule and patient-loading tray.

VISUAL PRIORITY: one magnificent attractive rescue protagonist. A strong three-dimensional heroic silhouette, small fierce architectural helmet, high broad shoulder line, a deep transverse breastplate, dark narrow mechanical waist, short quiet white upper thighs, very large heavy lower legs and wedge boots. Main shoulder width roughly 1.8–2 times narrowest waist, not a square torso with no waist. Low three-quarter view, both feet fully visible and grounded in a calm commanding stance. Right hand slightly open in readiness to receive a person; left hand a relaxed strong fist. No weapon, no winged angel styling. It must feel weighty and sophisticated, not cute or flat. Communicate a complete designed body BEFORE the individual vehicle identities.

COMPOSITION: landscape art plate on a warm-paper ivory background. The MAIN CLOSED-CHEST full-body hero occupies about 78 percent of the canvas width and almost the full height. Leave the upper/right margin for one SMALL functional close-up inset of the SAME chest with its front doors OPEN and a level patient stretcher entering. Inset roughly one fifth the scale of the hero, secondary and quiet. NO second full giant, no component lineup, no text, no letters, numbers, logos, arrows, captions or frames. Keep all toes, wing tips and equipment within the page.

CLOSED HERO CHEST — this is the central visual invention:
The intact medical capsule is seated HORIZONTALLY across the giant's chest, supported behind by a dark-blue cradle. Its closed outward-facing protective doors form a single broad, handsome steel-white BREASTPLATE: two large faceted armor leaves meeting on a clean central seam, beveling up slightly toward the shoulders and sloping inward below, with one deep teal transverse band outlining the lower contour. This is a powerful flat-arched / shallow shield chest symbol, NOT a flat rectangular bus stuck on the chest, NOT a gaping cargo box, NOT a glass cockpit, NOT a cross logo. A row of five small AMBER RECTANGULAR rescue lamps runs within the dark slim upper rim and becomes the team's characteristic horizontal mark. These outer protective doors enclose the unchanged level patient room; the interior remains inside. Large uninterrupted armor planes, sparse meaningful seams, a few protected black vents along the lower rim. No random torso grille clutter and no separately pasted vehicle cab noses on top of it.

HEAD AND SHOULDERS:
A compact navy rescue-commander helmet with white angular jaw guard, dark brow frame, narrow amber eyes, one short red central forehead ridge and broad layered temple plates. Original serious heroic head, not the five solo heads enlarged, no huge antenna fork, no baby face. Head clearly above the transverse chest and framed by the high shoulder yoke.
The tow truck's TWO substantial dark-blue articulated recovery arms fold outward and around the shoulder line to make a visible symmetrical structural shoulder yoke, their distinctive circular pivots and ivory/rust-red cowl plates preserved. They create a raised strong shoulder silhouette instead of long unstructured cranes sticking into the sky. Tow cab shell sections form handsome wide shoulder armor and navy/white forearm armor; both forearms feel substantial and carry angular silver-white wrist cuffs. One wrist integrates Bailing's folded patient-support tray, readable as a real rescue tool rather than a gun. Keep its fingers strong and fully articulated.

BACK, WAIST AND LEGS:
The transporter's actual open flat cargo deck rises behind the torso as a broad folded back platform. Its navy side rails and TWO rear loading ramps remain visible above/behind the shoulders as structural rectangular silhouettes, not feathery wings. Its cab/chassis portions form the navy hip frame and belt armor.
The FIRE unit's two actual red heat-shield panels unfold diagonally behind the upper shoulders, giving a restrained red double-chevron silhouette behind the navy yoke. Both silver-black water cannons are present and folded along these panels pointing rear/up, clearly water-cannon booms, not huge gun barrels. Rounded red tank sections remain partly visible at upper back / rear arms. No extra red wings beyond these two panels.
The ENGINEERING chassis divides into TWO truly thick yellow-and-navy lower legs and broad stable wedge boots. Recognizable dark wheels are nested along the outer/rear calves, and the FOUR original folding stabilizer legs lie along the calf/heel structures as visible bracing details. Big ochre-yellow vertical shin planes, dark navy sidewalls and toe/heel shapes, white small knee transition plates. Its crane boom is folded compactly along the rear spinal platform and the hook is secured, not hovering detached.
Bailing's remaining navy/white chassis and wheel bogies stay integrated at the chest cradle sides / rear hip frame, not turned into the patient room floor. Do not hang dozens of tiny wheels on every joint; retain the real assemblies where their size makes sense.

COLOR DESIGN: deep navy shoulder/arm/waist framework, one strong WHITE-and-DEEP-TEAL chest symbol, RED protected panels behind the shoulders, OCHRE-YELLOW large lower legs, restrained steel-white thighs and cuff planes, amber lamps as a narrow repeated accent. Five constituent colors are regional major masses, not rainbow confetti. Saturated rescue colors with realistic paint depth and slight age, no predominant warm-cream appliance shell. Dark joints have convincing occlusion and interlocking mechanical depth.

SMALL OPEN-CHEST INSET:
Show ONLY a three-quarter close-up of the upper torso. It is precisely the same white/teal chest breastplate; its two outer armor-door leaves slide sideways / lift clear, revealing a protected rectangular entrance with a LEVEL HORIZONTAL FLOOR, warm low night lamps and a stretcher on a broad outward loading platform. The outside hand aligns under the platform, supporting access. The doors must visibly be the same armor as on the main closed view. The patient room is intact; never split, tipped upright or replaced by a robot cockpit. A tiny attending medic can establish scale if helpful. This inset shows the functional alternate state and must not dominate the design.

RENDERING: accomplished hand-drawn project mecha illustration, fine varied dark-navy/black ink edges, richly articulated but controlled mechanical drawing, believable volume, layered hard-and-soft occlusion shadows, lightly weathered painted metal, subtle edge chips and dirt in selected seams. Use shading depth comparable to reference 3; do NOT mechanically restrict the image to two flat shadow colors. Large shapes first, little detail only where meaningful. Avoid plastic 3D product rendering, glossy toy surfaces, clean vector icons, round children's robot shapes, nonfunctional fantasy ornaments, glowing tubes, exaggerated panel clutter, lens flares or dramatic background.
This is a visual design proposal with coherent component provenance, not a claim of verified physical transformation.

FUNCTIONAL INSET:
A close three-quarter view of the SAME rectangular patient room and adjacent upper back support, cropped so the room is the focus. Its broad outward side door slides open. Inside, the floor stays horizontal and continuous, with warm low night lighting, a protected stretcher docking rail, and room for one tiny adult attendant beside a patient on a stretcher. The robot's patient-support platform is aligned LEVEL with the room floor, and a precise mechanical hand stabilizes the outer end. The loading path is visibly clear; no vertical doorway drop, no stairs, no patient capsule split into armor, no person entering a giant's mouth. Same white wall, teal lower stripe, dark upper window and amber lamps as the closed main view. The patient and clinician give scale, rendered simply and respectfully.

HEAD DETAIL:
One small three-quarter portrait, same helmet and face as the main figure. Show the slightly flared protective eave, angular cheek armor and restrained service lamps with mature industrial design. No alternate head, no option letters.

Style: highly accomplished hand-drawn mechanical character illustration, fine variable dark-navy ink, convincing painted steel volume and occlusion depth, muted metallic edges, restrained chips and warm paper. Strong big forms with designed planar transitions. Broad quiet armor surfaces contrast with articulated joints and cradle. Do not reduce to flat two-tone cel/vector art; do not turn into photoreal PBR or a shiny plastic toy. Every part feels substantial and usable. The character's authority comes from posture, clean geometry, stable load-bearing body and precise working hands.
